A callback-driven for-model loop would save only iteration while hiding policy. source_reason: Both clean up owned pending asyncio tasks by cancelling and awaiting, but their exception contracts differ: request gather cleanup suppresses ordinary exceptions as well as cancellation, whereas keepalive suppresses only cancellation. A scoped reusable cleanup helper can make that difference explicit.
boundary: Own cancel_pending_tasks(tasks, suppress_errors=False) in a lightweight core async utility, promoted from the existing pending-gather helper. Snapshot only unfinished tasks once, cancel every selected task before awaiting any, then await sequentially; always suppress CancelledError, and suppress Exception only when requested. Common request processing passes suppress_errors=True; keepalive passes its singleton only when pending is not None and uses False. Preserve completed-task exclusion, no shielding, and existing outer finally scopes. A task that converts cancellation to ValueError must be swallowed for gather cleanup but propagate from keepalive. Leave heartbeat creation, idle timeouts, yield timing, pending=None reset, and disabled-interval direct __anext__ unchanged. This pending-only helper is distinct from the all-task gather/drain contract in packet 5.

source_reason: Only SHA-256 plus conversion of the first eight digest bytes is shared. Scheduling offsets and constrained MCP names have unrelated seeds, guards and output contracts.
boundary: A generic hash_u64(seed) could preserve UTF-8, big endian and first-eight truncation but is a two-line utility without a shared domain owner. Keep nonpositive windows returning before hashing, NUL job/identity separation, MCP empty-ID error, attempt-zero seed, retry suffix and constrained first character. Neither public function substitutes for the other.

source_reason: The common queue push is already owned by async_rpush_pipeline and RedisPipelineRpushOperation. The rest is a one-batch safe requeue versus draining and tracking multiple spend queues with recovery.
boundary: A pure JSON rpush-operation builder could wrap RedisPipelineRpushOperation(key=key, values=[safe_dumps(payload)]), but adds only tiny utility. Keep list(items) normalization in tool restore, its no-cache/empty guards and uncaught push failures. Spend must drain queues sequentially, convert window payloads, push all nonempty operations together once, preserve aligned service types, restore original in-memory aggregates on push failure, and emit gauges only after success. Do not call the tool restore method once per spend queue or reuse its retry policy.

source_reason: Both already call the DB exception owner for connection and transport classification. Permanent-fault wording and stale-reader fallback are different policies built from these predicates.

Do not use is_permanent_database_fault to decide fallback: a non-transport infrastructure error is permanent but must be re-raised by the writer-read path. A union predicate would save only the two existing predicate calls and must retain their evaluation order if introduced; it does not consolidate the async writer retry, warning, or revision race check.

source_reason: run_server already imports and calls resolve_database_token_auth; both use token_auth_flag_enabled. The CLI block is startup override/export wiring, whereas the resolver builds the strategy from current environment. It is not a second token-strategy implementation.

CLI true flags short-circuit parsing potentially invalid environment values, then export True and apply writer URL before subsequent config/secret-manager setup. Preserve the later resolver call for PgBouncer.

source_reason: Skill visibility is already centralized in resolve_skill_visibility and SkillVisibility.allows. Archive metadata retrieval and marketplace detail retrieval expose distinct lookup and error contracts.
boundary: Do not replace marketplace lookup with _version_metadata: that helper uses PluginUploadStore, requires metadata.id, and deliberately answers 404 for hidden records. get_plugin queries the repository directly, answers 403 for an ungranted plugin, parses its manifest and wraps unexpected errors as 500. Keep visibility resolution after successful lookup and preserve each endpoint's status/body and caller auth.

source_reason: The policies are distinct, but each reaches a separately defined identical proxy-admin predicate. An existing resource_ownership.is_proxy_admin already owns precisely that role check, so a tiny partial reuse is available.
boundary: Import the existing is_proxy_admin predicate (aliasing if compatibility requires) into both owning endpoint modules; keep the guards local and synchronous. A non-admin with caller api_key is allowed for Gemini but forbidden with 403 for vector indexes. Preserve Gemini 401 text, admin short-circuit, data.get(api_key) truthiness and the vector operation-specific message. Do not replace either policy with the other or broaden to admin-viewer.

source_reason: async_pre_call_hook already calls _unmaskable_reason for diagnostics and indirectly through _mask_unwritable_instructions_pii_in_place. boundary: Keep the existing helper and dedicated instructions mask path. Preserve pre-call skip guards, inspection filtering, call_v2_guard timing, mask-before-advisory behavior, monitor permissiveness, scope-preserving write-back and final applied-header mutation.

source_reason: Best-effort CyberArk rollback and validated Vault update have different effects and failure contracts. Environment assignment is already shared through set_env_vars.

source_reason: Legacy generate and update custom hooks repeat coroutine validation, awaited invocation and deny-by-decision policy. source_reason: Both already share trust-aware HTTPS detection. The token cookie and OAuth state cookie deliberately have different browser accessibility, lifetime and optional-request rules.

source_reason: The identical blake2b(digest_size=8) to signed big-endian integer conversion can share a small deterministic advisory-key primitive. Normalization, naming and transaction semantics differ and are not reusable as a unit.

Pass exactly mcp_identifier:{lowercased_identifier} from the sorted/deduplicated/nonempty identifier loop, and exactly {user_id}:{server_id} from merge_user_env_vars, preserving byte encoding and existing namespace strings to remain compatible with concurrent old processes. Feed its remaining headers to merge_mcp_headers, preserving static-versus-forwarded precedence and empty dict/None shape. Retain the ORIGINAL per_server dictionary as the third return value when authorization exists. For an empty per_server dict the helper returns {} whereas without_header returns None; merge_mcp_headers treats both as absent and returns merged or None, so the public return shape stays identical.

source_reason: The resemblance is the ordinary GET/raise_for_status/json idiom. These have different transport owners, exception families, authentication handling, payload shape and query/timeout behavior; there is no shared prompt/team operation.

Preserve synchronous execution and the prompt caller cache/parse sequence; a transport abstraction solely for these two would exceed the shared behavior.

source_reason: The cancel-each-then-gather(return_exceptions=True) cleanup is identical and has a real resource-lifetime contract. Engine shutdown and concurrent catalog pagination can share that operation without sharing their workflows.

source_reason: Both use ProviderConfigManager.get_provider_model_info, already the common provider lookup owner. Credential selection and absence handling differ materially.
boundary: Keep affinity fallback model-aware and returning None for missing model info or NotImplementedError from get_api_key. source_reason: The shared slice is an error notice followed by a reason-limited close. It can have one owner in realtime_errors, but the current send-failure contracts differ and are part of the extraction interface.
boundary: Introduce realtime_errors.send_error_and_close(websocket, message, error_type, close_code, fallback, send_failure_policy). Reuse realtime_error_event and websocket_close_reason. The handshake mode catches only Exception from send, then closes (BaseException from send still skips close). The denial mode closes in finally even on cancellation, then propagates the original send failure unless close itself fails. Preserve close-error propagation in both. Resolve the handshake status-derived code lazily at close time after the send attempt, preserving its import/error timing. Pass server_error/status-derived code for handshake; pass already-redacted denial_message, permission_error and 1008 for policy denial. Keep authorization await and False return in _send_to_backend and all backend transformation/usage mutations outside. This is partial orchestration reuse, not replacing _send_to_backend with the handshake helper.

source_reason: A narrow synchronous normalization operation is duplicated: UTF-8 decoding and retaining the substring beginning at the first data: delimiter. Iterator mechanics and provider-specific parsing are not equivalent and need not be extracted.

BaseModelResponseIterator calls it only inside its existing bytes branch; string and non-string chunks remain untouched, blank skipping stays after normalization, and ValueError/UnicodeDecodeError stays inside the parsing-error wrapper after the upstream await. Do not use the existing strip_sse_data_from_chunk as a replacement: it removes the delimiter rather than finding and retaining it. Keep sync/async iteration, stop signals and response-id state outside the helper.

source_reason: The tests cover different failure boundaries: a mocked transport ValueError must make one attempt, whereas stream=True fails at the public entry point before transport. pytest.raises and a user message are not a meaningful shared operation.

source_reason: Both construct ModelResponse/Usage test data, but the shared content is constructor syntax. The fixture supplies fixed complete response metadata while the sequential-request test intentionally varies usage, IDs and costs and omits those fields.

Do not reuse the same mutable fixture response across iterations or move on_request/on_response or cost patch scopes: each request must record fresh metrics and preserve the accumulated 0.45 assertion.

source_reason: ConversationInfo composition already has one owner, _compose_conversation_info. The remaining overlap is an inactive-service guard and await get_state followed by that helper.

If added, call it with the captured EventService (not a second ID lookup), preserve sequential awaits in search and its filter/sort/pagination, and leave missing-ID None and inactive-service errors in callers.

source_reason: Both native-output arms already call _create_output_config_for_response_format. The response_format translator additionally chooses native versus synthetic-tool output, handles thinking, sets json_mode and possibly fake_stream. The Anthropic-format adapter only accepts a native format; its caller warns and drops an unsupported format rather than injecting a tool. The common serialization policy has an existing owner.
boundary: Keep _create_output_config_for_response_format as the shared boundary. Do not merge input parsing, capability selection, synthetic-tool fallback or streaming flags. An unsupported Anthropic output_config.format must not acquire the response_format fallback.

source_reason: These operations use the same typed cache but own different cache lifetimes. get_org_object reads a normal or with-budget key, queries the database on a miss, distinguishes missing rows from outages, and writes DEFAULT_IN_MEMORY_TTL. _keep_last_known_org preserves a separate last-known value only when absent locally, using the management-object TTL. get_org_object_for_request composes them and consults the last-known value on a database outage.
boundary: No useful extraction between these endpoints. Keep local-only retention, separate keys, TTLs and absence/outage handling explicit. A generic get-or-set wrapper would obscure when stale organization restrictions are retained.

source_reason: The two independently reached auth paths repeat the full expiry rule: parse an ISO string or datetime, assign UTC to naive values, compare strictly before the current UTC time, and raise the same expired-key 401. This is substantive authorization policy. Other shared operations already have helpers, and the surrounding workflows differ: custom checks are opt-in, attach user budgets independently, and use a different budget-skip predicate and key-budget gate from virtual-key validation.
boundary: Extract the expiry normalization/comparison and expired-key exception construction from lines 4737-4751 and 3142-3160 into one helper. Pass the already chosen error param and current time explicitly; preserve the virtual-key debug log and each call position. Retain strict <, malformed-date errors, timezone treatment, token-less custom-auth param="", and virtual-key api_key redaction. Do not merge budget orchestration, DB requirements, fallback recomputation, or the opt-in gates.

source_reason: Both cancel asynchronous work, but their callers establish different ownership. Request cleanup cancels only pending moderation/LLM tasks, awaits each, and suppresses child cancellation and ordinary exceptions. Prisma shutdown cancels its tracked snapshot, gathers outcomes, then waits for a reconnect lock; it is registered in an AsyncExitStack after marking the client closing. Collapsing the await mechanisms would also change how cancellation of the cleanup coroutine behaves.
boundary: Keep the request-finally cleanup and engine shutdown distinct. The common task.cancel loop is a tiny idiom, not enough to justify an abstraction with pending-selection, await, cancellation and reconnect policies. Do not drop the in-flight reconnect barrier or consume already-completed request tasks differently.

source_reason: Restore pushes a serialized batch back to Redis after a write proven safe to retry; drain pops bounded list entries, validates each batch and aggregates by tool name. Their caller first drains, attempts the database write, and restores only on a requeue-safe failure. Opposite effects on the same queue are not duplicate implementations.
boundary: Keep rpush restoration separate from lpop/validation/aggregation. Preserve the no-Redis return forms (None versus empty tuple), empty-input guard, dequeue cap and the caller's retry-safety gate.

source_reason: is_permanent_database_fault classifies nontransient infrastructure faults to choose 503 wording and chain priority. handle_db_exception is a startup/migration raise-or-tolerate policy that suppresses only connection failures when the configured flag allows it. Both already reuse is_database_connection_error, but one is a predicate and the other changes control flow.
boundary: No new shared error handler. Retain existing classification primitives. A transport or infrastructure failure must not become tolerable simply because it participates in the permanent/transient messaging classifier.

source_reason: resolve_database_token_auth only reads and validates environment toggles, then calls build_database_token_auth. The builder already owns mutually exclusive strategy selection, including conflict rejection and None when neither toggle is on. DatabaseURLSettings.token_auth also calls the builder with resolved booleans. There are not two independent strategy implementations.
boundary: Retain the environment adapter and shared builder. Do not make settings-based callers reread toggle environment variables; preserve read_replica forwarding and the conflicting-toggle error.

source_reason: resolve_database_token_auth delegates through build_database_token_auth to RdsIamTokenAuth.from_env only when IAM is selected. The former parses strategy toggles; the latter resolves a writer or replica region and strips whitespace. Azure selection and disabled auth never need the RDS constructor. The call chain already shares the RDS operation.
boundary: Keep strategy selection and RDS region loading at their current boundaries. No generic environment getter is warranted; flag validation and blank-region normalization are different rules.

source_reason: get_skill_version directly calls _version_metadata for current visibility and identity checks, then fetches a particular publication. List and archive routes use the same metadata helper. The helper hides absent/invisible skills with one 404, whereas the route has a separate missing-version 404 and response construction.
boundary: Keep current visibility authorization in _version_metadata. Preserve checking current metadata before loading a historical version, and distinguish skill absence from publication absence. No second extraction between these endpoints.

source_reason: Gemini agent CRUD allows ordinary authenticated callers when they supply their own provider key; only admins may use the environment fallback. Coordination Redis mutation requires the proxy-admin role regardless of any caller-supplied key, returning a different 403 response. Its read endpoint also has an explicit admin-view bypass. Matching role checks do not establish a common permission policy.
boundary: Keep the two guards distinct. A non-admin with api_key is the concrete counterexample: allowed by the Gemini guard and denied by Redis mutation. Preserve 401 versus 403 and the endpoint-specific response details.

source_reason: _metadata_object_or_error directly reuses _normalized_metadata_object and adapts its result: None becomes an empty object, success is copied, and ProxyException becomes a return value. Auth-body detachment uses that result to keep its copy safe, while request processing calls the strict normalizer after popping raw metadata so a 400 is not masked by logging failures.
boundary: Keep one normalizer and the explicit tolerant adapter. Do not turn a strict 400 into an empty object, propagate the tolerant error too early, or remove the defensive copy/None special case.

source_reason: update_cyberark_config already invokes _restore_cyberark_runtime after persistence failure. Restore reestablishes the previous environment and manager best-effort, clears a failed CyberArk manager, and may reactivate Hashicorp. Update performs authorization, merge/validation, initialization, persistence and audit. Its earlier initialization failure restores only the environment, a distinct existing boundary.
boundary: Retain the rollback helper and update workflow. Do not replace either initialization-failure or persistence-failure handling with a single generic initializer without proving manager state equivalence; keep fallback-manager recovery and audit ordering.

source_reason: The session token cookie is deliberately readable by dashboard JavaScript, has the framework default path, and no explicit expiry. The OAuth state cookie stores an encrypted per-flow blob under a random-handle name, is HttpOnly, expires after 600 seconds and uses the public base path. Both set SameSite=lax and a secure flag, but those shared options are convenience rather than a common cookie contract.
boundary: Keep named cookie policies. Do not unify HttpOnly, path, max_age or naming. Preserve the respective HTTPS resolution helpers and OAuth flow binding; a generic set_cookie wrapper would largely duplicate the framework API.

source_reason: MCP error_text_result renders an Exception into text content with is_error=True. The harness returns a structured HTTP/SSE error dictionary and requires an externally supplied message that callers sanitize against secrets. It also accepts BaseException. The only common operation is retrieving the exception class name.
boundary: Keep protocol encoders separate. In particular do not replace the harness's sanitized message with str(exc), or replace MCP TextContent and error flag with a nested HTTP error object.

source_reason: Both remove every casing of Authorization from a copied mapping. MCP already delegates filtering to without_header and additionally extracts the first incoming value for passthrough credential resolution. Databricks strips old Authorization before installing a resolved bearer. A small reusable filter is possible, but without_header returns None for an empty result and accepts string values, while Databricks must return an unpackable mapping and preserves object values.
boundary: At most promote a generic case-insensitive mapping filter, keeping MCP's None/empty adapter and credential extraction local. Databricks must still yield {} when only Authorization existed. Do not merge passthrough credential selection with Databricks bearer precedence.

source_reason: Both fetch prompt data but speak different APIs. Generic prompt management sends query parameters, returns raw JSON and wraps HTTP/JSON parse errors. Phoenix sanitizes a path identifier, validates and unwraps a typed data envelope, treats 404 as absence and gives special 401/403 diagnostics. Their callers compile different prompt representations and own distinct caches. HTTP get/raise_for_status/json is already client-library functionality.
boundary: No useful common prompt-fetch implementation. Preserve path sanitation, query parameters, client/header ownership, envelope validation and Phoenix absence semantics. An HTTP-JSON convenience wrapper would not own the important behavior.

source_reason: The async prompt fetcher sends authenticated query parameters via the PromptManagement client and returns JSON with contextual exceptions. _fetch_remote_bytes uses the UI client, a five-second timeout and raw bytes. Its actual consumer validates an autorouter catalog and falls back to a bundled catalog on failure. Their shared GET/status idiom does not imply a common domain operation.
boundary: Keep prompt fetching and remote catalog bytes separate. Preserve client pools, authentication, timeout, raw-byte versus JSON return types and error propagation to the bundled-catalog fallback.

source_reason: The cut-short stream handler calls _scan_released_pipeline_stream, which calls execute_steps, which invokes _run_step. Guardrail execution is already shared. The outer handler shields a scan of already released content and records failed-to-respond entries only for unsettled guardrails after scan failure; _run_step classifies one step, carries replacement data and copies logging information from a separate input.
boundary: Keep the executor as the shared owner. Retain cut-short shielding, reconstructed end-of-stream input and unsettled-only failure records outside single-step execution. Do not conflate fail/error outcomes with post-disconnect audit completion.

source_reason: clear_cache preserves ordinary live DB models and reloads through add_deployment_locked; reconciliation calls _delete_deployment to evict no-longer-desired IDs. Its direct deletion is confined to DB auto-router deployments so strategy registries can be rebuilt. _delete_deployment instead combines DB/config desired IDs and preserves config deployments when configuration is unavailable. The ordinary removal policy is already reused.
boundary: Keep ID reconciliation in _delete_deployment and the locked auto-router reset in clear_cache. Do not replace the narrow reset with deleting every DB deployment, merge the non-reentrant lock boundaries, or erase None-versus-empty desired-state semantics.

source_reason: _apply_streaming_chunk_hooks directly invokes ProxyLogging.async_post_call_streaming_hook. The logger derives pre-rewrite text for callbacks; the wrapper derives text again from the returned possibly modified chunk to accumulate emitted content. The logger also recognizes A2A dictionaries and can skip work when no hooks are active. The two string reads can observe different objects and are not redundant.
boundary: Retain hook dispatch in ProxyLogging and emitted-text accumulation in the wrapper. Do not cache the pre-hook response string as the post-hook string, or widen wrapper accumulation to A2A without a separate behavior change.

source_reason: collect_observed performs provider I/O, identity enrichment, per-repository duplicate checking, spend reads and connection cleanup. combine_observed merges completed connection snapshots, checks window/spend agreement, rejects duplicate URLs and deduplicates branch spend. Their caller intentionally collects each connection then combines it. Optional-issue flattening resembles a reusable fragment, but empty input and pull ordering differ.
boundary: No useful whole-period builder across these endpoints. Preserve duplicate identities (repo/number versus URL), sort keys (merged_at/repo/number versus merged_at/URL), branch-spend unknown propagation, and the empty-results issue distinction. A small optional-flatten helper alone would be convenience.

source_reason: Prisma tasks are asyncio tasks owned by the database client; stopping them cancels execution and waits for reconnect shutdown. A2A tasks are JSON protocol records in a response; _list_tasks_result_to maps dictionary items to a target wire version while preserving other fields and non-dictionary entries. The shared word tasks is a naming collision.
boundary: No extraction. Preserve cancellation/join side effects in Prisma and pure response-shape conversion in A2A, including unchanged return on a non-list tasks value.

source_reason: These are complementary pieces of an encryption affinity boundary, not duplicate fallback policies. The API-key path asks provider model info for get_api_key and tolerates NotImplementedError. The URL path asks a responses config for get_complete_url with API base and request parameters, tolerating specific routing/auth errors. The caller independently bypasses either resolver when that explicit value is supplied.
boundary: Keep separate typed provider-resolution operations. Do not catch the union of both exception sets, force both lookups when only one value is missing, or treat model-info and responses-config registries as interchangeable.

source_reason: Both endpoints implement the same meaningful failure-delivery sequence: optionally send a serialized error event, tolerate an ordinary send failure, then attempt close. This protects the close attempt when notification fails. Neither endpoint currently reuses the other. Upstream refusal additionally maps HTTP status and bounds the reason; proxy rejection owns optional error codes, debug logging and release of two request reservations in finally.
boundary: Extract only best-effort notification followed by close into a realtime I/O helper accepting a pre-serialized optional event, close code/reason and optional send-failure logging. Preserve catching Exception rather than BaseException, propagating close errors, and the no-event branch. Keep upstream status/reason formatting outside and leave the proxy's existing finally release order around the helper; do not infer new cleanup guarantees or change close-reason truncation.

source_reason: BaseModelResponseIterator.__anext__ repeatedly reads provider stream chunks, skips blanks, decodes bytes, parses SSE and distinguishes receive versus parse ValueErrors while preserving StopAsyncIteration. Harness _anext reads already typed Event values and converts only exhaustion into a None sentinel for a synchronous bridge. Reusing that exhaustion policy in the provider parser would change its iterator protocol.
boundary: No shared next-item wrapper. Preserve typed events versus raw stream parsing, StopAsyncIteration propagation versus None, and the provider's distinct error messages. The base sync/async parser may have a separate duplication opportunity, but it is not this pair.

source_reason: The pytest cases repeat identical LLM constructor settings and a one-message completion input. Their required assertions are deliberately opposite: a transient APIConnectionError followed by success must make two calls, while ValueError must propagate after one. The file already has a default_config fixture with matching retry values but a different service_id, and both tests currently instantiate their own LLM despite requesting it.
boundary: Reuse a local fresh-LLM fixture or factory for constructor settings, preserving test-service where observable. Keep side effects, exception context and call-count/response assertions in the separate tests. This is setup convenience, not evidence that the two test behaviors should merge.

source_reason: Telemetry's pytest fixture intentionally has empty choices and fixed model/time/usage so latency and accounting can be exercised independently. The hello-world helper builds an ordered tool-call then completion dialogue, embeds a temporary filesystem path and uses per-response usage/finish reasons. Its callers drive an agent/file-edit flow. A generic ModelResponse constructor wrapper would not consolidate an independently implemented behavior.
boundary: Keep the scenario fixtures separate. Preserve empty choices in telemetry, temporary path, tool arguments, response order and finish reasons in hello-world. Shared type construction alone is not a useful extraction.

source_reason: Both start with an active-service guard and event-service lookup; an existing get_event_service method already implements that exact lookup. get_conversation then reads state and composes metadata; resume_conversation starts a service and returns its truthiness. The pinned tree has GET/batch callers for get_conversation but no textual caller for resume_conversation; the run route calls get_event_service then run directly. This limits the demonstrated maintenance value.
boundary: At most reuse get_event_service for the guard/lookup. Keep None versus boolean return contracts, resume's truthiness check and start side effect, and get's state composition separate. Do not remove resume solely from the absence of a textual caller or confuse start with the route's run operation.
